title: Add login & user accounts
content:
## What you'll get

Your app will have sign-up and login pages so each person gets their own private space and data.

## Why you need accounts

Right now, everyone who visits your app sees the same thing. If you're building a to-do list, a journal, or anything where people should have their own private information, you need user accounts. Once someone logs in, the app knows who they are and can show them only their own tasks, posts, or whatever you're building.

<Callout type="note" title="Built in from day one">
Every Emergent app includes authentication automatically - no extra setup or billing required. You just describe what you want in chat and the AI wires it up.
</Callout>

## Add login with a prompt

Tell the AI what you want in plain English:

<Steps>
<Step title="Describe sign-up and login">
Type something like: *"Users should be able to sign up with email and password, then log in to see their dashboard."*

The AI will create login and sign-up pages, handle sessions, and make sure people stay logged in when they come back.
</Step>

<Step title="Protect your pages">
If you only want logged-in people to see certain pages, say: *"Make the dashboard page require login."*

Visitors who aren't signed in will be sent to the login page first.
</Step>

<Step title="Let people reset passwords">
Add: *"Let users reset their password if they forget it."*

The platform will email them a reset link automatically.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="Video coming soon">
A short screen recording will go here.
</Callout>

## Email or Google sign-in

Emergent supports two main ways for people to sign in:

- **Email and password** - the traditional way. Users pick a password and the app stores it securely (hashed, never in plain text). This works out of the box with zero configuration.
- **Google sign-in** - let people use their Google account instead of creating a new password. This requires you to set up credentials in the Google Cloud Console first (see [Google auth](/google-auth) for the step-by-step).

<Callout type="tip" title="Start simple">
Begin with email/password - it's instant. You can always add Google sign-in later if your users ask for it.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="Draft - needs review">
This section (other OAuth providers like Apple or GitHub) needs product confirmation before publishing.
</Callout>

## See your users

Once people start signing up, their accounts are stored in your app's database in a collection called `User`. You can ask the AI to show you a list:

*"Show me all registered users in an admin page."*

Each user record includes their email, when they signed up, and any extra fields you've added (like display name or profile picture). You can query this collection just like any other data in your app.

<Callout type="info" title="Screenshot coming soon">
Screenshot to be added.
</Callout>

## If something looks wrong

**People can't log in after signing up** - make sure you tested the sign-up flow yourself in preview mode. If password reset emails aren't arriving, check your spam folder or ask in chat: *"Why aren't password reset emails being delivered?"*

**You want to add profile pictures or other fields** - just describe it: *"Add a displayName field to users so they can choose a nickname."* The AI will extend the User collection and update the sign-up form.

**Sessions expire too fast** - Emergent Auth keeps people signed in using secure, server-side sessions. If the timeout doesn't suit your app, just describe what you want in chat: *"Keep users logged in longer between visits."*
